Rashi on Chullin 69a:10:1.hebrew: אבן פקועה דכוותיה - דאין [הולד] טעון שחיטה אלא משום חד אבר, וההוא אבר לא מישתרי בשחיטה, דלאו שחיטה היא, [וחתך ליה האי אבר ושרי]:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:10:1.english: With a ben pekua like it - For [the offspring] does not require slaughter except because of one limb, and that limb is not permitted through slaughter, since it is not [considered a valid] slaughter; [and one severs this limb and it is permitted]:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:10:2.hebrew: מבלבל זרעיה - ומיתסר כל הולד משום אותו אבר, ואליבא דחנניא קבעי לה:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:10:2.english: [His] seed is intermingled - and the entire offspring is prohibited on account of that limb, and he asks this in accordance with [the view of] Chananya:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:12:1.hebrew: לאו מכח חלב ודם - של אבוה קאתי, שאף החלב והדם הולידו:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:12:1.english: [Is it] not from the force of [forbidden] fat and blood - of its father [that] it comes, for the [forbidden] fat and blood also engendered [it]:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:12:2.hebrew: תרי איסורי אמרינן - דשרי, אבל חלב ודם ויוצא לא:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:12:2.english: We say two prohibitions - that it is permitted, but [forbidden] fat, blood, and [a limb that] went out [of its boundary] — no:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:13:1.english: And according to whom - are there three [prohibitions]?

Rashi on Chullin 69a:13:2.hebrew: אי לר"מ - דאמר איסור חלב נוהג בשליל, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:13:2.english: If [it is] according to Rabbi Meir - who says that the prohibition of forbidden fat applies to a fetus, as [stated] below:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:13:3.hebrew: איסור חלב ודם איכא איסור יוצא ליכא - דהא לר"מ אפי' מה שבפנים טעון שחיטה, כדקתני מתניתין (שם): "ומצא בה בן תשעה חי טעון שחיטה", הלכך ה"ל כשאר בהמה:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:13:3.english: There is a prohibition of [forbidden] fat and blood, [but] there is no prohibition of [a limb that] leaves - For according to Rabbi Meir, even what is inside [the womb] requires slaughter, as the Mishnah teaches (there): "And if he found a live nine-month [fetus] inside her, it requires slaughter"; therefore, it is like any other animal:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:14:1.hebrew: ואי כר' יהודה - בר פלוגתיה, דאמר אין טעון שחיטה מה שבפנים, ואיכא איסור יוצא שאין לו היתר; איסור חלב ליכא:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:14:1.english: And if [it is] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - his disputant, who says that what is inside [the womb] does not require slaughter, and [therefore] there is a prohibition of [a limb] that leaves [the womb], for it has no permission; [while] there is no prohibition of forbidden fat:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:15:1.english: Applies to the fetus - The sciatic nerve and the fat of a fetus are forbidden:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:16:1.hebrew: אלא - הא לא קמיבעיא ליה, דכל מכח לא אמרינן דליתסר משום שבא מכח איסור:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:16:1.english: Rather - he had no dilemma about this, for we do not say [that] anything [coming] from the influence [of something forbidden] is forbidden because it comes from the influence of a prohibition:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:17:1.hebrew: את חלבו - אם נקבה היא וילדה והרי היא חולבת, חלבה מהו באכילה? והיינו "לזרעו" דקאמר, שאין החלב בא עד שתלד:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:17:1.english: Its milk - If it is a female and it gave birth and is now producing milk, what is [the law regarding] its milk with respect to consumption? And this is [what the Gemara meant by] "its offspring" that it said [earlier], for the milk does not come until it gives birth:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:19:1.hebrew: בהמה בבהמה - שדיא בהמה דרישא אבהמה דסיפא, ודרוש הכי: בהמה הנמצאת בבהמה תאכלו:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:19:1.english: An animal in an animal - Cast [the word] "animal" [behemah] from the beginning [of the verse] onto "in an animal" [babehemah] at the end [of the verse], and expound [it] thus: "An animal that is found inside an animal, you may eat."

Rashi on Chullin 69a:1:1.english: This is the principle - It is our Mishnah:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:1:2.hebrew: דבר שאינו גופה - אלא מן העובר ונמצא בתוכה, מותר:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:1:2.english: Something that is not [part of] its body - rather, [something that is] from the fetus and is found inside [the mother] is permitted:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:1:3.hebrew: לאתויי מאי - אי חותך מן העובר, תנא ליה; אלא לאו לאתויי כה"ג, דנשאר מיעוט העובר בפנים ורובו יצא מחותך:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:1:3.english: What [does it come] to include - If [it comes to include] cutting from the fetus, [the Mishnah] has already taught it; rather, is it not to include a case like this, where a minority of the fetus remained inside [the womb] and its majority came out cut [in pieces]?

Rashi on Chullin 69a:20:1.english: If that is so - since a fetus is called an animal:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:20:2.hebrew: ימירו - אם הביא בהמת חולין אצל בהמת קדשים מעוברת, ואמר: "הרי זו תמורת עובר של זו", תהא תמורה; דהא גבי תמורה, בהמה כתיב (ויקרא כז): "ואם המר ימיר בהמה בבהמה":
Rashi on Chullin 69a:20:2.english: They should [be able to] substitute - if one brought a non-sacred animal next to a pregnant consecrated animal and said, "This is hereby a substitute for the fetus of this [animal]," it should become a substitute [and be consecrated]; for regarding substitution, "animal" is written (Leviticus 27[:10]): "And if he shall indeed substitute an animal for an animal":

Rashi on Chullin 69a:21:1.hebrew: אין ממירין - כלומר, אם המיר, אין מומר, דכל ממירין דתמורה דיעבד הוא, כדאמרן בשמעתא קמייתא דפרקא קמא (לעיל חולין ב.):
Rashi on Chullin 69a:21:1.english: One cannot substitute - That is to say, if one [did] substitute, it is not substituted [i.e., the substitution does not take effect], for every [instance of] "cannot substitute" in [Tractate] Temurah is [even] after the fact, as we said in the first discussion of the first chapter (above, Chullin 2a):

Rashi on Chullin 69a:21:2.english: Not limbs for fetuses - [one cannot declare] a limb of this non-sacred animal [to be] a substitute in place of a fetus of this consecrated animal:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:21:3.english: And [one cannot substitute] fetuses for limbs - [Saying, "Let] the fetus of this non-sacred animal [be] a substitute for the leg of this consecrated animal":

Rashi on Chullin 69a:21:4.english: And [one cannot substitute] a fetus and a limb for whole [animals] - Thus, [we see that] they are not called an "animal":

Rashi on Chullin 69a:22:1.hebrew: אלא - לאו מבהמה נפקא, אלא מכל נפקא, והכי דריש: "כל מפרסת פרסה בבהמה תאכלו", כלומר, כל אשר תמצא בבהמה — אכול:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:22:1.english: Rather - it is not derived from [the word] "animal," rather it is derived from [the word] "every." And this is how [the Gemara] expounds [the verse]: "Every [animal] that parts the hoof ... in an animal, you may eat" — that is to say, whatever you find in an animal, eat:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:23:1.hebrew: אותה תאכלו כשהיא שלמה - אכול כל הנמצא בתוכה, אבל כשהיא חסרה — שהנמצא בתוכה מגופה הוא שנחסר ממנה — לא תאכל הנמצא:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:23:1.english: "It you may eat" [means] when it is whole - eat everything that is found inside it; but when it is lacking — [meaning] that what is found inside it is from its [own] body that was removed from it — you may not eat what is found [inside]:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:24:1.english: If that is so - that you expound [the words] "every" [and] "in the animal":

Rashi on Chullin 69a:2:1.hebrew: לאתויי קלוט - אפי' הנמצא שלם במעי פרה:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:2:1.english: To include [one with] non-cloven hooves - Even [one] that is found whole inside the womb of a cow:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:3:1.english: A fetus extended - [a fetus] of a peace-offering [extended] its foreleg at the time of its mother's slaughter in the [Temple] courtyard:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:3:2.english: What is [the law] - For the wall of the [Temple] courtyard to be a boundary for it, to permit it through the slaughter of the mother:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:4:1.hebrew: ותבעי לך קדשים קלים בירושלים - כגון עובר שלמים שהוציא את ידו בירושלים והחזירה, והכניסוה לעזרה ושחטוה, ותבעי לך אליבא דמ"ד יש לידה לאברים ולא מהניא חזרה: מי מהניא ליה חומה דלא ליהוי בשר בשדה, דהא חומת העיר הויא מחיצה לקדשים קלים? וליכא לאוקמא בשוחט שלמים בירושלים והוציא העובר את ידו לחוץ, דא"כ אף הבהמה אסורה משום שוחט קדשים בחוץ:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:4:1.english: And you should raise [the dilemma] regarding offerings of lesser sanctity within Jerusalem - For example, a fetus of a peace-offering that extended its foreleg [while] in Jerusalem and pulled it back in, and they brought [the mother] into the Temple Courtyard and slaughtered it. And you should raise the dilemma according to the one who says that "birth" applies to limbs [individually] and pulling [the limb] back in is not effective: does the wall [of Jerusalem] avail for it so that it is not [considered] "flesh in the field" [outside its permitted boundary], since the wall of the city is a [valid] boundary for offerings of lesser sanctity? And it is impossible to establish [the dilemma] as [a case of] one who slaughters a peace-offering in Jerusalem and the fetus extended its foreleg outside [the city], for if so, even the [mother] animal is forbidden on account of slaughtering consecrated offerings outside [the Temple Courtyard]:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:4:2.english: Is its mother - and not the wall [of Jerusalem]:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:6:1.hebrew: מי מצטרף סימן ראשון לסימן שני - גרסינן. והכי מיבעי ליה: סימן ראשון, כשנשחטה בעוד אבר זה בתוכה, היה בא להתיר אף באכילה; ומשיצא, אין חתיכת סימן שני בא על אבר זה אלא לטהרו מידי נבלה, כדאמרן לעיל "וחכ"א מגע טרפה שחוטה" — מי מצטרף סימן ראשון, שבא לו לטהר ולהתיר, עם זה שאינו בא אלא לטהר, להועילו מיהא לטהר, הואיל ושניהם שוין בכך:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:6:1.english: Does the first siman combine with the second siman - This is our reading. And this is what he is asking: The first siman, when [the mother] was slaughtered while this limb was still inside her, came to permit [the limb] even for consumption; and once [the limb] emerged, the cutting of the second siman comes upon this limb only to render it pure from [the impurity of] a carcass, as we said above, "And the Sages say: [it has the status of] contact with a slaughtered tereifah" — does the first siman, which came to render it pure and to permit [it for consumption], combine with this [second siman], which comes only to render [it] pure, to be effective for it at least to render [it] pure, since both of them are equal in this [respect]?

Rashi on Chullin 69a:6:2.hebrew: או - דלמא כיון דיש חילוק ביניהם, לא מצטרף ראשון — שהוא נשחט לשני דברים — עם השני, שאינו אלא לטהרו מידי נבלה, ואין כאן שחיטה שלמה לטהרו:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:6:2.english: Or [not] - Perhaps, since there is a difference between them, the first [siman] — which is slaughtered for two purposes — does not combine with the second [siman], which is only [effective] to render it pure from [the impurity of] a carcass, and [thus] there is no complete slaughter here to render it pure:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:6:3.hebrew: אם מצטרף סימן ראשון לשני להתיר באכילה - כל העובר והבהמה, ולא אמרינן שחיטה חלוקה היא ואין שחיטה לא בזו ולא בזו — לא תועיל לאבר לטהרו מידי נבלה:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:6:3.english: If the first siman combines with the second to permit for consumption - [namely,] the entire fetus and the animal, and we do not say [that] it is a divided slaughter and [that] there is no [valid] slaughter with either this [siman] or that [siman] — will it not be effective for the limb to render it pure from [the impurity of] a carcass:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:7:1.hebrew: מהו לחוש לזרעו - של עובר זה שהוציא ידו, ונשחטה אמו, והוציאוהו חי, וגדל ובא על הבהמה והוליד — מהו שיאסר אבר כיוצא בו הנולד ממנו:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:7:1.english: What is [the law regarding] being concerned for its offspring - of this fetus that extended its foreleg, and its mother was slaughtered, and they took it out alive, and it grew up, mated with an animal, and sired [offspring] — what is [the law] regarding whether the corresponding limb born from it is forbidden:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:9:1.hebrew: אפי' בן פקועה דעלמא - שלא הוציא את ידו, וגדל והוליד, נמי אסור כל הולד:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:9:1.english: Even a regular ben pekua - [one] that did not stick out its foreleg, and grew up and fathered [offspring from a full-fledged animal], the entire offspring is also forbidden:

Rashi on Chullin 69a:9:2.english: As Rav Mesharshiyya says: According to the statement of the one who says [that] one is concerned for the father's seed - This [refers to] Chananya, in [the chapter entitled] Oto Ve'et Beno (below, Chullin 78b):

Rashi on Chullin 69a:9:3.hebrew: אין לו תקנה - שמצד אביו אין טעון שחיטה, כדתנן במתני' (שם דף עד.): "וחכ"א שחיטת אמו מטהרתו"; ומצד אמו טעון שחיטה, וסימניו אינן סימנין, דהא פלגיה כשחוטין דמו, ואי נמי ה"ל בר סימן א', ובהמה צריכה רוב שנים:
Rashi on Chullin 69a:9:3.english: Has no rectification - For from its father's side it does not require slaughter, as we learned in the Mishnah (there, 74a): "And the Sages say: Its mother's slaughter renders it permitted"; while from its mother's side it requires slaughter, yet its signs [of slaughter — the trachea and esophagus] are not [valid] signs, for half of it is as [meat] already slaughtered, and furthermore it is [like] a creature with [only] one sign, whereas an animal requires [the slaughter of] the majority of two [signs]:

Tosafot on Chullin 69a:10:1.english: That [it] came upon a ben pekua like it - in which there is the prohibition of yotzei [having emerged from the womb] in one limb:

Tosafot on Chullin 69a:12:1.hebrew: או דלמא תרי איסורי אמרינן - לאו דוקא תרי איסורי אמרינן, דאיכא נמי איסור גיד הנשה:
Tosafot on Chullin 69a:12:1.english: Or perhaps we say two prohibitions - [It is] not literally two prohibitions [that] we say, for there is also the prohibition of the sciatic nerve:

Tosafot on Chullin 69a:12:2.hebrew: תלתא לא אמרינן - תימה, מאי קמיבעיא ליה? והא קי"ל (לעיל חולין דף נח.) דזה וזה גורם מותר:
Tosafot on Chullin 69a:12:2.english: Three [prohibitions] we do not say - [This is] astonishing: what is his dilemma? Why, we hold (above, Chullin 58a) that [something caused by] both this and that is permitted:

Tosafot on Chullin 69a:24:1.hebrew: אלמה א"ר יוחנן השוחט בהמה ומצא בה דמות יונה אסור באכילה בעינן פרסות וליכא - נראה דוקא נקט "דמות יונה", שהוא אסור גם כשיצא לאויר העולם לפי שאינו מתקיים; אבל מצא בה בהמה גמורה שראוי להיות מותר, ורגליה רגלי יונה, או שאין לה רגלים כלל, מותרת, דלא ממעט ר' יוחנן מידי שראוי להיות מותר כשיצא לאויר העולם; דההיא חשיב כמפריס פרסה להיות ניתר בשחיטת אמו, כמו שחשוב כמפריס פרסה כשיצא לאויר העולם, דלא על חנם תפס ר' יוחנן "דמות יונה", ולא נקט "עובר שרגליו דמות יונה" או "עובר שאין לו רגלים". וכי פריך "קלוט במעי אמו ליתסר", אליבא דרבי שמעון דוקא פריך, דאסר ליה כשיצא לאויר העולם, כדפרישית לעיל:
Tosafot on Chullin 69a:24:1.english: Why did Rabbi Yoḥanan say: One who slaughters an animal and finds a dove-shaped [fetus] in it, it is prohibited for consumption? We require hooves, and there are none - It seems that [Rabbi Yoḥanan] specifically mentioned "a dove-shaped [fetus]," which is prohibited even when it emerges into the air of the world because it is not viable; but [if] one found in it a fully formed animal that is fit to be permitted, and its feet are the feet of a dove, or it has no feet at all, it is permitted, for Rabbi Yoḥanan does not exclude anything that is fit to be permitted when it emerges into the air of the world; for that [animal] is considered like one with split hooves so as to be permitted through the slaughter of its mother, just as it is considered like one with split hooves when it emerges into the air of the world — for it was not for nothing that Rabbi Yoḥanan chose "a dove-shaped [fetus]" and did not mention "a fetus whose feet are dove-shaped" or "a fetus that has no feet." And when [the Gemara] asks, "Let an uncloven-hoofed [animal] in its mother's womb be prohibited," it asks specifically according to Rabbi Shimon, who prohibits it when it emerges into the air of the world, as I explained above:

Tosafot on Chullin 69a:4:1.hebrew: ותבעי לך קדשים קלים בירושלים - רב חנניא הוה מיבעי ליה בעזרה, משום דחשיבה מחיצה יותר אפי' לענין שחיטת קדשים קלים; ומיהו בנולד כולו בעזרה לא קא מיבעי ליה, דפשיטא דטעון שחיטה:
Tosafot on Chullin 69a:4:1.english: And [why don't] you raise [the dilemma regarding] offerings of lesser sanctity within Jerusalem - Rav Ḥananya raised his dilemma [specifically] regarding [the Temple] courtyard, because [the courtyard] is considered more of a boundary, even with respect to the slaughter of offerings of lesser sanctity; however, regarding [a fetus] that was born entirely in the courtyard, he did not raise the dilemma, for it is obvious that it requires [its own] slaughter:
